absent: Numeric values of leading and trailing markers, trailing marker size, legacy magic and all feature masks.
Full memory layouts of register, header, task, soft environment and legacy structures.
Semantics of conversion, fault resolution, disable state, supervisor mask, clear, trace and capability query helpers.
Hardware semantics of extended save and restore operations and control registers.
Configuration and feature enumeration meanings for 32-bit, emulation and 64-bit builds.

findings.text: copy_fpstate_to_sigframe is the signal delivery save interface taking separate legacy and extended user buffers plus total size and protection key value and reporting success as boolean.
fpu__restore_sig is the signal return restore interface taking a user buffer and 32-bit frame indicator and reporting success, clearing user states on null input or failure.

fpu__alloc_mathframe reserves an aligned signal math area below a given stack pointer and reports locations and total size, while fpu__get_fpstate_size reports worst case size including trailing marker and legacy storage when relevant.

get_xsave_addr_user locates the user buffer area for a numbered extended feature, copy_sigframe_from_user_to_xstate transfers a user signal frame into task extended state with key handling, and fpstate_clear_xstate_component clears one component area.
fpu__resume_cpu restores extended control state on CPU resume and arch_set_user_pkey_access updates current protection key rights for a numbered key from abstract disable requests.
xsaves and xrstors save and restore independent components selected by a mask under validation.

An extended signal frame is accepted only when its leading marker matches, its claimed size lies between a legacy plus header minimum and both the task user size and its claimed extended size, and its trailing marker matches; otherwise it is treated as legacy only with cleared marker, legacy size and base feature set plus a trace event.
Software reserved bytes record leading marker, total user size, user feature set and extended size that grows by trailing marker size and additionally by legacy storage for 32-bit frames.

Signal save epilog writes software bytes into the reserved area, appends trailing marker when extended save is present, and unconditionally marks base features present in the user header so legacy modifications are observed.

User signal save uses the task user feature set, optionally narrowed to features needing write under dynamic sizing, validates against disable state, performs a privileged extended save to the user buffer, then updates key representation.
Key propagation is a no-op without OS key support; otherwise it marks the key feature present in the user header and stores the supplied key value into that feature area.

When hardware floating point is absent the save path synthesizes a legacy environment through soft emulation; otherwise it validates accessibility, clears the user header when extended save is present, and retries after clearing the target on fault.
User restore dispatches on processor capability among extended restore, fast save restore and legacy restore, and initializes user features absent from the restore mask from the initial state.
Restore masks the requested set to enabled user features, refreshes disable state, restores supervisor components separately when register state is not loaded, and marks state active on success.

The compatibility restore path preserves supervisor state, invalidates loaded registers, copies extended or legacy state, folds legacy environment into extended registers, enforces control word validity strictly on 64-bit and by masking on 32-bit, and narrows the memory header to user requested plus supervisor features before safe restore.
Signal frame size equals task user size, extended by trailing marker size when extended save is present and by legacy register storage for 32-bit fast save frames.

Per-feature offset, size and order tables use all-ones as uninitialized sentinel, flag bit zero denotes supervisor and bit one denotes 64-byte alignment, and a defined aggregate mask enumerates features handled in the initial state.

CPU resume restores the user feature mask into the extended control register when extended save is present, restores supervisor plus independent masks into the supervisor control register when compacted save is present, and restores the dynamic disable register from current task state when sizing is dynamic.

Independent component operations require compacted save support and a non-empty mask confined to independent features, otherwise they warn and do nothing, and hardware errors during those operations warn.

User key update requires OS key support and a valid key number, translates abstract access and write disable requests into per-key preservation and update of the hardware rights register, and reports invalid input as an error.
Feature order helpers iterate in uncompacted offset order and compare features by their offsets to establish canonical layout order.

Direct register save and restore to or from user memory holds the register lock, ensures registers are loaded for the current task, and disables page faults across hardware access, releasing in reverse order; fault retry drops the lock before resolving the fault and reacquires.

The signal frame software descriptor logically carries leading marker, extended size, feature set and claimed state size; the user extended area carries a header with a feature present bitmap plus per-feature slots located by per-feature offsets.
Extended state metadata consists of parallel per-feature tables for human names, processor capability dependencies, offsets, sizes, flags and uncompacted order, all indexed by feature number.

Signal save progresses from accessibility and header preparation through load assurance and hardware save attempt to legacy header and software epilog completion, with a fault recovery loop that clears and retries before failing.

Signal restore progresses from frame validation and feature set extraction through either direct register restore or invalidated copy plus fold plus safe restore, ending in active marking on success and user state clearing on failure.
Signal handling enters extended state management through the save interface during delivery and the restore interface during return, while CPU bringup or resume enters through the resume hook.

Faults or invalid contents in user signal memory can cause save or restore failure, partial hardware register modification, or supervisor state loss if invalidation and separate supervisor restore are omitted; non page fault errors during restore are fatal.

Accessing a disabled feature address yields null, restore with invalid control bits must be rejected or masked by word size, and independent operations with empty or non-independent masks warn without acting.

Signal frame compatibility relies on leading and trailing marker values, trailing marker size, base feature mask, legacy magic and status handling, 64-byte frame alignment, per-feature capability bindings and the ordered feature name list.
Supervisor and alignment flag bits and the aggregate initial handled feature mask define which components are supervisor managed, alignment constrained and preinitialized.
